simple.meaning: אֵיתָן (ʼêythân) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “permanence ; hence (concrete) permanent ; specifically a chieftain.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 49:24. The surrounding context includes priesthood, city, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵיתָן (H386) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֵיתָן (ʼêythân) / H386 is traced through Genesis 49:24, Exodus 14:27, Numbers 24:21, Deuteronomy 21:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it. Yahweh overthrew the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.
He looked at the Kenite, and took up his parable, and said,
The elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a valley with running water, which is neither plowed nor sown, and shall break the heifer’s neck there in the valley.
He is chastened also with pain on his bed,
You opened up spring and stream.

Behold, I will bring a nation on you from far away, house of Israel,” says Yahweh. “It is a mighty nation. It is an ancient nation, a nation whose language you don’t know and don’t understand what they say.
“Behold, he will come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation:
Behold, the enemy will come up like a lion
But let justice roll on like rivers,

definitions.short: permanence ; hence (concrete) permanent ; specifically a chieftain
definitions.full: H386. ethan I. אֵתָן אֵיתָן, adjective perennial, ever-flowing , figurative permanent, as substantive steady flow, permanence; — absolute אֵיתָן Gen 49:24 8 t.; אֵתָן Job 33:19 ; suffix אֵיתָנוֺ Exod 14:27 ; plural אֵיתָנִים Job 12:19 ; אֵתָנִים 1Kin 8:2 ; Micah 6:2 ; (in form, an 'elative,' Ew § 162 b = Arabic comparative and superlative); — 1 ever-flowing (opposed to אַכְזָב ), אֵיתָן נַחַל Amos 5:24 an ever-flowing wady, Deut 21:4 (see Dr); as substantive in אֵיתָּן נַהֲרוֺת Psa 74:15 rivers of steady flow ; as substantive also Exod 14:27 (J), the sea returned לְאֵיתָנוֺ to its steady flow , הָאֵיתָנִים יֶרַת 1Kin 8:2 month of steady flowings = 7th mo., Oct.-;Nov. (post-Biblical Tisri). 2 figurative permanent, enduring הוּא אֵיתָן גּוֺי Jer 5:15 , i.e. a nation whose numbers never dwindle or fail, imperishable , א עֲצָמָיו ׳וְרִיב Job 33:19 Kt the strife of his bones is constant , Gen 49:24 his bow abode ׳בְּא as an enduring, firm , one, ׳א מוֺשָֽׁבְךָ Num 24:21 (|| בַּסֶּלַע שִׂים ), אֵיתָן נְוֵה Jer 49:19 = 50:44 an abode of permanency (of Edom, and Babylon, suddenly depopulated by foe, figured as lion); ארץ מוסדי האיתנים Micah 6:2 ye ever-enduring ones, the foundations of the earth (but read probably with We הַאֲזִינוּ ), Job 12:19 יְסַלֵּף אֵיתָנִים he subverteth them that are firmly seated (i.e. men established in hereditary offices or dignities). Very uncertain is Prov 13:15 אֵיתָן בִּגְדִים דֶּרֶךְ , perhaps firm, hard, rugged (Ew De Hi Now according to Str. the text is corrupt).
definitions.rootNote: or (shortened) אֵתָן ; from an unused root (meaning to continue );
